items.title: 美國為何突然出手救日元？貝森特最怕亞洲貨幣競貶
items.title_en: Why Is the United States Suddenly Acting to Save the Yen? Bessent’s Biggest Fear Is an Asian Currency Devaluation Race
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周二 (4 日) 表示，美國之所以罕見加入日本的買進日元行動，是因為日元持續疲弱可能迫使其他亞洲國家競相讓本幣貶值，進而動搖區域及全球金融市場。
貝森特接受《CNBC》節目「Squawk Box」訪問時表示，穩定的日元不僅對美國重要，對整個亞洲也相當關鍵。他指出，日元若大幅貶值，可能對其他國家形成貨幣貶值壓力，目前韓元已出現劇烈波動，人民幣匯率也存在遭到低估的疑慮。
貝森特表示，考量日本的貿易規模、經濟體量，以及日本對全球儲蓄市場的貢獻，維持日元穩定至關重要。日本政府了解這一點，美方也樂於支持日本落實相關政策，共同協助穩定亞洲市場。
此次行動是美國罕見出手支撐另一種主要貨幣，凸顯華府擔心日元長期疲弱不僅會推高日本進口成本與通膨，也可能壓迫其他亞洲貨幣，甚至將金融動盪擴散至全球市場。
在這次美日聯合干預中，美國財政部動用外匯存底出售歐元，再將所得資金用於買進日元。貝森特表示，他已向歐洲官員保證，出售歐元只是美國外匯存底的重新配置，並非刻意打壓歐元。
貝森特指出，美日是在日元遭到「嚴重低估」後，聯手進場買進日元。兩國政府此前一直保持密切聯繫，華府也相信日本將採取適當政策，使日元逐步回到較為正常的水準。
不過，貝森特坦言，干預只能在短期內抑制匯市波動，無法單獨決定日元的長期走勢。他強調，政府可以透過干預向市場發出訊號，但真正扭轉匯率方向的仍是政策。
貝森特拒絕直接評論日本央行是否應該升息，僅表示日本官員必須在干預後推出更廣泛的政策，處理造成日元走弱的根本因素。美國決定參與此次行動，正是因為對日本接下來的政策路線抱持樂觀態度。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday (the 4th) that the United States’ rare decision to join Japan in buying yen is driven by the concern that a persistently weak yen could force other Asian countries to competitively devalue their own currencies, thereby destabilising regional and global financial markets.

In an interview on CNBC’s “Squawk Box,” Bessent stressed that a stable yen is not only important for the United States but also crucial for the entire Asian region. He warned that a sharp depreciation of the yen could create downward pressure on other currencies – the Korean won is already showing extreme volatility, and there are doubts that the renminbi is being undervalued.

Bessent noted that, given Japan’s trade size, economic weight and its contribution to the global savings market, keeping the yen stable is essential. The Japanese government understands this, and the U.S. is happy to support Japan in implementing related policies to help stabilise Asian markets jointly.

This intervention marks a rare instance of the United States backing another major currency, highlighting Washington’s worry that prolonged yen weakness would not only raise Japan’s import costs and inflation but also pressure other Asian currencies and potentially spread financial turbulence worldwide.

In the joint U.S.-Japan intervention, the Treasury used foreign‑exchange reserves to sell euros and then used the proceeds to buy yen. Bessent said he has assured European officials that the euro sales are merely a reallocation of U.S. reserves, not an intentional move to suppress the euro.

Bessent explained that the U.S. and Japan entered the market after the yen was deemed “severely undervalued.” The two governments have been in close contact, and Washington believes Japan will adopt appropriate policies to gradually bring the yen back to a more normal level.

However, Bessent admitted that intervention can only curb short‑term FX volatility and cannot determine the yen’s long‑term trajectory on its own. He emphasized that while governments can signal intentions through intervention, the real driver of exchange‑rate direction remains policy.

Bessent declined to comment directly on whether the Bank of Japan should raise rates, saying only that Japanese officials need to follow the intervention with broader measures that address the underlying factors behind the yen’s weakness. The United States chose to participate because it is optimistic about Japan’s forthcoming policy path.

items.title: 〈台幣〉出口商+央行救場 量縮貶幅收斂險守32.5元大關
items.title_en: Exporters and Central Bank Bailout Narrow TWD Depreciation, Guarding the 32.5‑Per‑Dollar Barrier
paras: 台股今 (4) 日走勢震盪小跌作收，新台幣兌美元盤中再度面臨 32.5 元關卡保衛戰，但央行持續介入穩匯，加上出口商擴大拋匯，帶動匯價拉升至平盤附近，以 32.447 元作收，微貶 0.9 分，為連 2 貶，台北與元太外匯市場總成交值萎縮至 24.7 億美元。
新台幣兌美元今天開盤報 32.447 元，午後在外資擴大匯出下，匯價一度下探至 32.495 元，距 32.5 元大關僅一步之遙。隨著匯價來到相對低點，出口商隨即進場擴大拋匯，台幣貶幅縮小；加上央行尾盤適時調節，終場幾乎回吐午後所有貶幅，收在 32.447 元。
觀察主要貨幣今天對美元表現，根據央行統計，美元指數上漲 0.19%，日元歷經昨日的飆漲後，今天回跌 0.65%，韓元貶值 0.33%，星幣貶值 0.12%，新台幣小貶 0.03%，人民幣則小升 0.03%，主要亞幣偏貶。
美股昨日強勢大漲，但台股今日開盤後一度下跌近 500 點，台積電領跌，電子權值股漲跌互見，不過，矽光子、PCB、記憶體等族群獲得資金青睞，大盤跌幅收斂，終場收在 43360.66 點，跌 25.75 點。
paras_en: Taiwan’s stock market edged lower in a volatile session today, while the New Taiwan dollar (NTD) faced another test at the 32.5 per USD level. The central bank’s continued intervention helped stabilize the exchange rate, and exporters’ increased foreign‑currency sales pushed the rate back toward the flat‑rate area, closing at 32.447 NTD per USD, a modest 0.9‑point decline and the second consecutive drop. The total turnover in Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets shrank to US$2.47 billion.

The NTD opened at 32.447 per USD. In the afternoon, foreign investors expanded their currency outflows, briefly driving the rate to 32.495, just a hair away from the 32.5 threshold. As the rate hit this relative low, exporters stepped in with larger currency sales, narrowing the depreciation. Coupled with timely adjustments by the central bank near the close, the market almost fully recovered the afternoon’s losses, ending again at 32.447.

Looking at major currencies against the dollar, central‑bank data show the US Dollar Index rose 0.19%. The Japanese yen, after yesterday’s surge, fell 0.65% today. The Korean won slipped 0.33%, the Singapore dollar 0.12%, the New Taiwan dollar a modest 0.03% decline, while the Chinese yuan edged up 0.03%, indicating a general weakening of Asian currencies.

U.S. equities rallied strongly yesterday, but Taiwan’s market fell nearly 500 points after the open, led down by TSMC. Electronics heavyweights showed mixed moves, while sectors such as silicon photonics, printed circuit boards and memory chips attracted buying. The overall market’s decline narrowed, closing at 43,360.66 points, down 25.75 points.

items.title: 美日聯手救日元藏盤算？貝森特盯上美債、日本升息與5500億美元投資
items.title_en: US and Japan Unite to Rescue the Yen: A Calculated Move?
paras: 美國與日本日前數十年來首度聯手買進日元，美國總統川普稱此舉是「友誼的象徵」，財政部長貝森特也宣稱，川普政府願意協助值得信賴的夥伴。不過，多名分析師認為，美方出手恐怕並非單純援助日本，背後還牽涉美債殖利率、日本央行升息、5500 億美元對美投資承諾，以及貿易與國防支出等多重盤算。
國際金融協會 (IIF) 資深經濟學家 Jonathan Fortun 直言，川普向來不會提供「免費午餐」。除了協助立場保守的日本首相高市早苗穩定局勢，美國也可能藉此要求日本加快對美投資，並在後續貿易及國防談判中作出更多讓步。

美債市場才是貝森特真正關切

分析人士指出，美國上周五加入日本買進日元，最明確的理由，是避免日本金融市場動盪蔓延至規模達 31 兆美元的美國公債市場。貝森特一直將 10 年期美債殖利率視為重要指標，而該殖利率上周五升至他上任以來最高水準，恰好與美日干預匯市發生在同一天。
日本是美國公債最大海外持有國。貝森特周日特別提到，日本可透過特定機制取得美元並買進日元，無須出售手中的美債。此舉有助避免日本為捍衛日元而拋售美債，進一步推高美國借貸成本。
大西洋理事會分析主管 Charles Lichfield 表示，相較於地緣政治盤算，防止美債殖利率急升，很可能才是華府更優先的目標。今年 1 月日本公債遭到拋售並波及美債時，貝森特也曾公開敦促日本財務大臣片山皋月控制市場動盪。
經濟學家認為，貝森特接下來幾乎肯定會要求日本央行進一步升息，以支撐日元並減少日債殖利率上升對美債的外溢效應。瑞穗證券資深市場經濟學家松尾祐介表示，協調干預匯市與施壓日本央行升息，可以視為同一套政策方案，最終目的都是阻止日本殖利率上升推高美債殖利率。
貝森特去年便曾批評日本央行在對抗通膨方面落後情勢，並呼籲日本政府給予央行升息空間。他上周五再次點名日本央行，表示期待 8 月與總裁植田和男會面。美國財政部最新匯率報告也指出，日本推動貨幣政策正常化，有助穩定通膨預期並降低匯率過度波動。
匯市目前已提高升息押注，隔夜交換市場顯示，日本央行 9 月升息機率接近五成，10 月前升息機率則約九成。不過，高市早苗長期支持貨幣寬鬆，可能使升息步伐面臨政治阻力。

華府或藉機追討投資與國防承諾

除了金融市場穩定，美國也可能利用這次罕見的匯率合作，要求日本加速履行去年 9 月承諾的 5500 億美元對美投資方案。該協議是日本換取美國降低關稅的重要條件，但目前專案簽署速度緩慢，其中包括軟銀集團支持、規模 330 億美元的俄亥俄州燃氣發電廠。
Lichfield 指出，若美國希望日本持續赴美投資，就必須確保日本負擔得起；日元過度疲弱，反而會增加日本企業與政府兌換美元、執行投資計畫的成本。因此，扶持日元既可穩定市場，也有助日本完成投資承諾。
日本今年稍晚還將修訂三份關鍵國家安全文件，可能為華府施壓提高國防支出提供機會。日本目前國防支出目標約占國內生產毛額 (GDP) 的 2%，美國則多次要求北約及其他盟友將比重提高至 3.5% 左右，未來不排除對日本提出類似要求。
分析人士認為，美日聯手買進日元，短期可替日本央行下一次升息爭取時間，避免匯率與債券市場失序；但華府提供支援後，也取得更多談判籌碼。這場被川普形容為「友誼」的匯市合作，最終代價可能落在升息、投資、貿易及國防承諾上。
paras_en: The US and Japan have recently joined forces to buy yen for the first time in decades, with US President Trump calling the move a 'symbol of friendship'. Treasury Secretary Bensen also stated that the Trump administration is willing to assist trustworthy partners. However, many analysts believe that the US's actions may not be solely to aid Japan, but also involve multiple calculations including US bond yields, the Bank of Japan's interest rate hike, a $550 billion investment pledge, and trade and defense spending.

Jonathan Fortun, a senior economist at the Institute of International Finance (IIF), said that Trump would not provide 'free lunch'. In addition to helping Japanese Prime Minister Kishida Fumio stabilize the situation, the US may also use this opportunity to request that Japan accelerate its investments in the US and make more concessions in subsequent trade and defense negotiations.

Analysts point out that the most obvious reason for the US to join Japan in buying yen last Friday was to prevent the turmoil in Japan's financial market from spreading to the $31 trillion US bond market. Bensen has always regarded the 10-year US bond yield as an important indicator, and the yield rose to its highest level since he took office on the same day as the US-Japan intervention in the foreign exchange market.

Japan is the largest foreign holder of US bonds. Bensen mentioned on Sunday that Japan can obtain dollars and buy yen through a specific mechanism without selling its US bonds. This move helps prevent Japan from selling US bonds to defend the yen, which would further increase the US borrowing cost.

Charles Lichfield, director of analysis at the Atlantic Council, said that compared to geopolitical calculations, preventing a sharp rise in US bond yields is likely to be Washington's more pressing goal. When Japanese bonds were sold off and affected US bonds in January, Bensen also publicly urged Japanese Finance Minister Shunichi Suzuki to control market volatility.

Economists believe that Bensen will almost certainly ask the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates further to support the yen and reduce the spillover effect of rising Japanese bond yields on US bonds. Matsuo Yuji, a senior market economist at Mizuho Securities, said that coordinated intervention in the foreign exchange market and pressure on the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates can be seen as part of the same policy package, with the ultimate goal of preventing a rise in Japanese yields from pushing up US bond yields.

Bensen had previously criticized the Bank of Japan for lagging behind in fighting inflation and called on the Japanese government to give the central bank room to raise interest rates. He again mentioned the Bank of Japan last Friday, saying he looks forward to meeting with Governor Haruhiko Kuroda in August. The US Treasury's latest foreign exchange report also stated that Japan's efforts to normalize monetary policy will help stabilize inflation expectations and reduce excessive exchange rate fluctuations.

The foreign exchange market has already increased its bets on an interest rate hike, with the overnight swap market showing a nearly 50% chance of a rate hike by the Bank of Japan in September and a 90% chance by October. However, Prime Minister Kishida's long-term support for monetary easing may make the pace of rate hikes face political resistance.

Washington may use this opportunity to demand that Japan accelerate its investment and defense commitments. In addition to financial market stability, the US may also use this rare currency cooperation to request that Japan speed up its fulfillment of the $550 billion investment plan in the US pledged last September. The agreement is a key condition for Japan to obtain US tariff reductions, but the project signing pace is slow, including a $33 billion gas-fired power plant in Ohio supported by SoftBank.

Lichfield pointed out that if the US wants Japan to continue investing in the US, it must ensure that Japan can afford it; an overly weak yen would increase the cost for Japanese companies and the government to exchange dollars and execute investment plans. Therefore, supporting the yen can stabilize the market and help Japan fulfill its investment commitments.

Japan will revise three key national security documents later this year, which may provide an opportunity for Washington to pressure Japan to increase its defense spending. Japan's current defense spending target is around 2% of its GDP, while the US has repeatedly asked NATO and other allies to increase their spending to around 3.5%; it is not ruled out that similar demands will be made on Japan in the future.

Analysts believe that the US-Japan joint purchase of yen can give the Bank of Japan time to raise interest rates and avoid disorder in the exchange rate and bond markets in the short term; however, after Washington provides support, it will also gain more bargaining chips. The cost of this 'friendly' currency cooperation, as described by Trump, may ultimately fall on interest rates, investment, trade, and defense commitments.

items.title: 日元空頭部位逼近2024年高點！套利交易捲土重來  逆轉風險將有多大？
items.title_en: Yen Shorts Approach 2024 High as Carry Trades Make a Comeback
paras: 今年以來，隨著日元持續疲弱、美日利差再度走闊，「借日元買美元資產」的套利交易規模明顯回潮，日本離岸金融帳戶淨資產截至5月突破2024年底高點、攀至95兆日元。
根據芝商所(CME)數據顯示，日元兌美元非商業淨空頭部位上月底大約15萬口合約，達2024年7月高點八成以上，擁擠度直逼兩年前引發全球股災的極端水位。
日本日前聯手美國介入匯市，估算投入約8.45兆日元(逾500億美元)，推升美元兌日元匯率自163高點回落至157附近，空頭遭重挫但未瓦解。
目前，市場關切2024年8月式的套利崩盤會否重演，主流機構判斷短期逆轉機率偏低，但部位過度集中下的「觸發式平倉」仍是今年下半年全球資本市場最大的尾部風險。

專家認為，三大邏輯支撐著「低逆轉風險」。一，宏觀環境不同於2024年8月(當時美非農驟冷、降息預期飆升)；當前美國經濟維持韌性，油價二次反彈拖慢通膨回落。聯準會(Fed)上周三(7月29日)以9比3維持利率於3.5%—3.75%不變、內部鷹派聲浪未消，美元與美債長端殖利率易強難弱，套利利差(美日約250—275bp)仍具吸引力；二，本輪科技股回檔屬漲多估值消化與部位再平衡，非AI敘事證偽或美國基本面轉壞，風險偏好未劇烈扭轉，暫不構成集中平倉壓力；三，日元疲軟主因並非純套利，而是日本財政擴張加劇債務可續疑慮、市場質疑日本央行(BOJ)獨立性，加上中東油價透過能源進口成本打擊日本貿易條件，結構性貶值動能獨立於套利交易之外。
然而「低機率」不等於「無衝擊」。BOJ上周五(7月31日)維持1%利率不變，總裁植田和男坦言通膨超標風險上升、匯率傳導增強，年內再升息一次已成基準情景，歐洲央行(ECB)上月也按兵不動，但9月升息懸念未解，英國央行也6比3鷹派僵持。
專家指出，一旦後續出現三大觸發點，美國經濟數據超預期走弱帶崩美債殖利率、AI族群深跌推高波動、日本財務省二度大手筆干預，高度擁擠的空頭恐瞬間反向踩踏，重演2024年8月式跨市場連鎖去槓桿。
地緣政治層面，美伊圍繞荷姆茲海峽反覆衝突，該水路牽動日本90%以上原油進口，任何通行風險都經「油價→通膨→美債利率→日元」路徑放大波動。
綜合來看，套利交易當下處於「收益尚可、部位危險」狀態。投資人短期無須恐慌性平倉，但須把美國經濟拐點、BOJ升息節奏、荷姆茲海峽局勢列為三盞紅燈，畢竟空頭部位已回到歷史高點附近。
paras_en: Since the beginning of the year, the yen has continued to weaken, and the US-Japan interest rate differential has widened again, leading to a significant rebound in carry trade volumes, with Japanese offshore financial accounts' net assets reaching a record high of 95 trillion yen as of May, surpassing the 2024 year-end high.

According to data from the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), the non-commercial net short yen position at the end of last month was approximately 150,000 contracts, exceeding 80% of the July 2024 high, with the crowdedness approaching the extreme levels that triggered the global stock market crash two years ago.

Japan recently intervened in the foreign exchange market in conjunction with the US, estimated to have injected around 8.45 trillion yen (over $500 billion), pushing the US dollar-yen exchange rate from 163 to around 157, causing significant losses for shorts but not eliminating them.

The market is currently concerned about the possibility of a repeat of the August 2024 carry trade collapse, with mainstream institutions judging the short-term reversal probability to be low, but the 'trigger-style liquidation' of over-concentrated positions remains the largest tail risk in global capital markets for the second half of the year.

Experts believe that three major logical supports the 'low reversal risk'. First, the macro environment is different from August 2024 (when US non-farm payrolls suddenly cooled and interest rate expectations soared); currently, the US economy maintains its resilience, and the second round of oil price rebound slows down the decline in inflation. The Federal Reserve (Fed) maintained its interest rate at 3.5% to 3.75% last Wednesday (July 29) with a 9-3 vote, and the internal hawkish voices have not dissipated, making the dollar and long-term US Treasury yields strong and weak, respectively, and the carry trade spread (around 250-275bp) remains attractive.

Second, this round of tech stock decline is a digestion of overvaluation and rebalancing of positions, and non-AI narrative evidence or a deterioration in US fundamentals have not caused a significant shift in risk appetite, and there is no pressure for concentrated liquidation.

Third, the yen's weakness is not solely due to carry trade, but rather the Japanese government's expansion of fiscal spending, which has exacerbated debt sustainability concerns, and the market's doubts about the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) independence, as well as the impact of Middle East oil prices on Japan's trade conditions through energy import costs, making structural depreciation independent of carry trade.

However, 'low probability' does not mean 'no impact'. The BOJ maintained its 1% interest rate unchanged last Friday (July 31), with Governor Kazuo Ueda acknowledging the rising risk of inflation exceeding the target, and the exchange rate transmission increasing, making a rate hike in the year a baseline scenario, with the European Central Bank (ECB) also maintaining its stance, but the 9% rate hike expectation in September remains, and the Bank of England also had a 6-3 hawkish stalemate.

Experts point out that if the three trigger points appear, the US economic data will unexpectedly weaken, triggering a collapse in US Treasury yields, AI stocks will plummet, and the Japanese Ministry of Finance will intervene again, the highly crowded short positions will be suddenly trampled, and the August 2024-style cross-market chain reaction will be repeated.

From a geopolitical perspective, the US-Iran conflict surrounding the Hormuz Strait has repeatedly escalated, with the waterway affecting 90% of Japan's oil imports, and any passage risk will be amplified through the 'oil price -> inflation -> US Treasury yields -> yen' channel.

In summary, the carry trade is currently in a state of 'profits are still available, but positions are risky'. Investors do not need to panic liquidate in the short term, but they should pay attention to the US economic turning point, the BOJ's rate hike pace, and the Hormuz Strait situation, as the short positions have returned to historical highs.

items.title: 不是護日元是議價！專家：天下沒有免費午餐　華府「友誼信號」背後藏三大盤算
items.title_en: Not About Protecting the Yen, It's About Bargaining! Experts: No Free Lunch—Washington’s “Friendship Signal” Hides Three Big Calculations
paras: 美國財政部上周五 (7 月 31 日) 協同日本財務省直接買入日元，為 1998 年來雙邊首見、2011 年後多邊框架外再度聯手護匯市，因日元兌美元匯率創近 40 年低，美國總統川普把行動包裝成「數十年來首次聯手捍衛日元的友誼信號」，財長貝森特稱「為值得信賴的夥伴提供支持」。
但華府智庫與市場幾乎一面倒質疑。國際金融協會 (IIF) 高級經濟學家 Jonathan Fortun Vargas 說：「天下沒有免費午餐，我們懂川普風格。」
大西洋理事會經濟前瞻與分析主任 Charles Lichfield 則點破核心，稱華府優先要務是在防止美債殖利率飆升，遠高於地緣作秀。
首先，日本是美債最大外國持有者，若東京為撐日元拋售美債換美元，31 兆美元美債市場將遭連鎖賣壓，10 年期美債殖利率上周五正好觸及美國財長貝森特上任以來最高。
貝森特周日 (2 日) 發文特意點出 FIMA Repo 機制，讓日本抵押美債換美元流動性、不必真拋持倉，等於把「救日元」與「穩美債」綁同一條船。
其次，華府要日本兌現 5500 億美元對美投資承諾，貿易談判再要讓步；日本下半年重訂國安優先順序，軍費加碼料成川普下一張牌。同時，日相高市早苗支持率滑落，華府護匯亦有鞏固同屬保守陣營領導人之意，套路類似去年對阿根廷。
最後，貝森特屢批日本央行 (BOJ) 抗通膨太慢，將在本月會見 BOJ 總裁植田和男。
瑞穗證券資深市場經濟學家 Yusuke Matsuo 指出，協調干預＋逼 BOJ 升息是同一套拳，目標是阻止日本國債殖利率暴衝外溢燒到美債，市場押注 BOJ 下月升息機率已逼近 50%、10 月約 90%。
截至周二 (4 日) 上午，日元仍穩居高於干預前水位，但「友誼」能撐多久，取決於 BOJ 何時升息、日相高市早苗會否再擴張財政及美債殖利率曲線是否會買單。
paras_en: On Friday, July 31, the U.S. Treasury, together with Japan’s Ministry of Finance, directly bought yen – the first bilateral joint intervention since 1998 and the first multilateral‑framework‑free cooperation since 2011 – to support the foreign‑exchange market as the yen‑dollar rate fell to a near‑40‑year low. President Trump framed the move as a “friendship signal” marking the first joint defense of the yen in decades, and Treasury Secretary Yellen said it was “support for a trustworthy partner.”

But think‑tanks and markets in Washington almost uniformly questioned the move. International Institute of Finance senior economist Jonathan Fortun Vargas said, “There’s no such thing as a free lunch; we understand Trump’s style.”
Atlantic Council senior economist Charles Lichfield cut to the core, stating that Washington’s top priority is preventing U.S. Treasury yields from spiking, far above any geopolitical showmanship.

First, Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries. If Tokyo were to sell U.S. bonds for dollars to prop up the yen, the $31 trillion Treasury market would face a cascade of selling pressure, and 10‑year Treasury yields hit their highest level since Yellen took office last Friday.

Yellen’s Sunday (the 2nd) post specifically highlighted the FIMA Repo mechanism, which lets Japan pledge Treasuries for dollar liquidity without actually liquidating its holdings—effectively tying “saving the yen” to “stabilizing U.S. bonds” on the same boat.

Second, Washington wants Japan to fulfill its $550 billion investment commitment to the United States and to make further concessions in trade talks; Japan’s mid‑year reshuffle of national‑security priorities and a boost in defense spending are expected to become Trump’s next bargaining chip. At the same time, support for Prime Minister Kishida is slipping, and Washington’s currency support also serves to shore up a fellow conservative leader, a tactic similar to last year’s approach toward Argentina.
Finally, Yellen has repeatedly criticized the Bank of Japan for moving too slowly on inflation and is slated to meet BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda later this month.

Mizuho Securities senior market economist Yusuke Matsuo noted that coordinated intervention and pressuring the BOJ to raise rates are two sides of the same strategy, aimed at preventing Japanese government‑bond yields from spilling over and inflating U.S. Treasury yields. The market now sees the probability of a BOJ rate hike next month approaching 50 % and about 90 % for October.

As of Tuesday morning (the 4th), the yen remained above the level before the intervention, but how long the “friendship” can hold depends on when the BOJ raises rates, whether Prime Minister Kishida expands fiscal spending, and whether the Treasury‑yield curve will accommodate the move.
